tests.expectedOutput: {"res1": "I haven't sent any messages in this chat before this one - this is my first reply here.", "res2": [101], "res3": "My last message said the first prime number greater than 100 is 101.", "res4": "My last message was: \"I haven't sent any messages in this chat before this one - this is my first reply here.\""}

evaluationCriteria.judgePrompt:
This tests what a call can see depending on which thread it runs in. The same function, which asks "What was the last message from you?", is called three times: once at node level, once inside a `thread {}` block that already holds a question and answer, and once more at node level after that block.

Two rules decide every answer below. Calls at node level share one default conversation, so a later one sees the earlier one. A `thread {}` block is separate from that conversation in both directions.

You should see an object with the keys res1, res2, res3 and res4.

## res1 - node level, nothing before it
Nothing has been said yet, so the assistant must report that it has no earlier message. Accept any wording carrying that meaning: "this is my first reply", "there is nothing before this", "I have no access to previous conversations". The reason it gives does not matter.

## res2 - inside the thread block
The number 101, in an array: [101].

## res3 - inside the thread block, after res2
This call CAN see res2, so it must refer back to it: the answer has to mention 101, or the first prime greater than 100. This is the half that proves a thread carries its own history.

## res4 - node level again, after the block
Two things must hold, and both matter:
- It must recall res1. The default conversation survived the thread block, so the assistant should quote or paraphrase its own res1 reply. An answer claiming it has no earlier message is WRONG here.
- It must NOT mention 101 or the prime-number question. Those were said inside the thread block; seeing them here would mean the block leaked out.

The Expected output is one recorded run. Judge meaning, never wording.
